mainTopic: Where the blood of a slaughtered animal may flow, and slaughtering 'for the sake of' an offering (נידר ונידב)
overview: The amud begins with the end of a משנה about where the blood of a slaughtered animal may flow. The worry is that people will think the slaughterer is serving idols or copying the מינים. רבא explains that a pool of water is allowed only when the water is murky, so no reflection shows. אביי and רבא then argue about how to read the משנה's rule on a hole in the ground. A ברייתא supports רבא: never slaughter straight into a hole, beside it is fine at home, and in the marketplace it is forbidden because of 'ובחקתיהם לא תלכו'. A new משנה then rules that slaughtering 'for the sake of' an offering that can be vowed or donated ruins the שחיטה, while naming an offering that comes only from obligation does not. The גמרא explains how אשם תלוי and פסח fit this rule. Several אמוראים then limit the rulings: the case of blemished animals, a man who owes a חטאת, a man who has an offering at home, and a man with a wife. The amud ends with the גמרא asking 'פשיטא?' on רבי אבהו's answer, and the reply comes on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the משנה: not imitating the מינים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by explaining why one may not make a hole for the blood in the marketplace: it would look like copying the מינים.
steps.simpleTranslation: …so that he will not appear to imitate the heretics.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of the משנה. They give the reason behind the last rule: one must not make a blood-hole in the marketplace, so he won't look like the מינים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed a person to make a hole inside his house for the blood. In the marketplace this is forbidden, because the מינים slaughtered this way in public as part of their worship. Doing the same thing in public would look like joining their practice.

keyTerms.meaning: He will imitate or copy
Heretics; a group whose religious practices the משנה does not want people to appear to copy

phrases.english: he will (appear to) imitate the heretics.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Conclusion of the משנה that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not make a hole for the blood in the marketplace, because it looks like imitating the מינים.

steps.title: Why may one not slaughter into seas?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and explains why slaughtering into seas is forbidden: people will think he is slaughtering to the angel of the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'One may not slaughter, neither into…' etc. What is different about seas, that one may not slaughter into them? It is because people will say: he is slaughtering to the angel of the sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts on the משנה and asks why slaughtering into seas is forbidden. It gives the reason: onlookers will think he is serving the angel of the sea. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is not about the blood itself. It is about appearances: it could look like עבודה זרה to the 'prince' of the sea. Once this reason is stated, the גמרא can test it against the משנה's permission for a pool of water.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
What is different? Asks why one case is treated differently
Seas
The angel or heavenly 'prince' of the sea

phrases.english: GEMARA:
'One may not slaughter, neither into…' etc.
phrases.notes: The full משנה says: not into seas, rivers or vessels, but one may slaughter into a round pit holding water.

phrases.english: What is different about (slaughtering) into seas, that one may not?
Because people will say: he is slaughtering to the angel of the sea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's analysis of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the reason for the ban on slaughtering into seas?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Onlookers will think he is slaughtering to the angel of the sea.

steps.title: A pool of water should also be forbidden because of the reflection
steps.stepSummary: If appearances matter, slaughtering into a pool of water should also be banned, since people will say he is slaughtering to his own reflection.
steps.simpleTranslation: Into a pool of water too, people will say: he is slaughtering to his reflection!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's permission to slaughter into a round pit of water. By the same reasoning, people might think he is worshipping his reflection in the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason from the last step was 'what people will think.' That reason seems to apply to the pool too, since a man bending over water sees his own image. So why does the משנה allow it?

keyTerms.meaning: A round pit or hollow holding water
Also, too
Reflection, a person's image in water

phrases.english: Into a round pit of water too,
people will say: he is slaughtering to (his) reflection!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְתוֹךְ עוּגָה שֶׁל מַיִם נָמֵי אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason from step 2 to challenge the משנה's permission for a pool
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to slaughter into a round pit of water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'what people will think' reason applies here too, because of the reflection.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה speaks of murky water
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the משנה allows a pool only when the water is murky, so no reflection can be seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They taught this about murky water.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. The משנה's permission is only for murky water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In murky water no reflection shows, so no one could think he is slaughtering to his image. The משנה's permission is narrowed to that case. With clear water, the concern would apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Murky, cloudy (water)
They taught; refers to what the משנה stated

steps.whatToRemember: Seas are forbidden because of the 'angel of the sea.' A pool is allowed only if the water is murky, so there is no reflection.

phrases.english: Rava said: They taught (this) about murky (water).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה allows any pool of water, which would raise the reflection problem
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה allows only murky water, where there is no reflection

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict itself about a hole
steps.stepSummary: The משנה first says never to slaughter into a hole at all, then allows making a hole in one's house. That looks like a contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One may not slaughter into a hole' etc. But you said one may not slaughter into a hole at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה and points out an internal contradiction. The משנה bans a hole completely, yet it then allows a hole in the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'not into a hole at all.' Then it said a person may make a hole in his house for the blood. Both statements cannot be true unless they speak about different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A small hole or pit in the ground
But didn't you say? Points to a contradiction
At all

phrases.english: 'One may not slaughter into a hole' etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: but one may make a hole inside his house so the blood flows into it.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמְרַתְּ: אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין לַגּוּמָּא כְּלָל?
phrases.english: But you said: one may not slaughter into a hole at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמְרַתְּ: אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין לַגּוּמָּא כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the hole clause of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to make a hole in one's house
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It contradicts the משנה's earlier blanket ban on slaughtering into a hole.

steps.title: אביי: the first clause is about a hole in the marketplace
steps.stepSummary: אביי resolves the contradiction: the full ban is about a hole in the marketplace, while the permission is for a hole in the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The first clause is about a hole in the marketplace.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction by splitting the cases. The רישא's total ban is about the marketplace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ban applies only in public, there is no conflict with allowing a hole at home. The two statements now speak about two different places.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא
Marketplace, a public place

phrases.english: Abaye said: The first clause is about a hole in the marketplace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): splitting the two clauses into different places
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on a hole applies everywhere, which contradicts the permission at home
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban is about the marketplace, and the permission is about the house

steps.title: רבא: the סיפא shows the רישא is not about the marketplace
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי. The סיפא mentions the marketplace separately, which shows the רישא was not talking about the marketplace.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But since the latter clause teaches 'and in the marketplace he may not do so,' this implies that in the first clause we are not dealing with the marketplace!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's answer using the wording of the משנה itself. The משנה brings up the marketplace only later, in the סיפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רישא were already about the marketplace, the סיפא would not need to add 'and in the marketplace he may not do so.' Since the סיפא introduces the marketplace as a new point, the רישא must be about somewhere else. So אביי's answer seems not to fit the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a משנה or ברייתא
By implication; it follows from this
We are dealing with

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא is saying the marketplace is allowed. He agrees it is forbidden. He is only arguing that the רישא cannot be the place where the משנה teaches that.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא מִדְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא ״וּבַשּׁוּק לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה כֵּן״,
phrases.english: But from the fact that the latter clause teaches 'and in the marketplace he may not do so,'
it implies that in the first clause we are not dealing with the marketplace!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer from step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the רישא is about a hole in the marketplace
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא introduces the marketplace as a new case. That implies the רישא was not about the marketplace.

steps.title: רבא rereads the משנה as one flowing rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the משנה differently. Slaughtering into a hole is banned everywhere. In a courtyard he may slaughter next to the hole and let the blood flow in, but not in the marketplace.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said the משנה means this: you may never slaughter straight into a hole. If someone wants to keep his courtyard clean, he makes a spot beside the hole, slaughters there, and the blood runs down into the hole. In the marketplace he should not even do that, so he will not look like he is copying the מינין.
steps.whatsHappening: Since אביי's answer was knocked down, רבא gives his own reading of the משנה. He says it is one continuous rule, not a contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three levels. Slaughtering directly into a hole is always banned. Slaughtering beside the hole and letting the blood flow in is allowed in your own courtyard. That same method is banned in the marketplace, because in public it looks like the practice of the מינין. This solves step 7's problem, because the marketplace really is a separate, new case in the סיפא.

keyTerms.meaning: To clean, or to keep clean (here: keep the courtyard free of blood)
At all, in any way
Flows, trickles

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's reading: never directly into a hole. Beside the hole is allowed at home. In the marketplace, not even beside it.
steps.confusionAlert: The courtyard permission is not slaughtering INTO the hole. He slaughters next to it, and the blood only flows in afterward.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
This is what [the Mishnah] is saying:
One may not slaughter into a hole at all,
and one who wants to keep his courtyard clean,
how does he do it?
He makes a spot outside the hole and slaughters there,
and the blood flows and runs down into the hole.
And in the marketplace he should not do this,
so that he will not imitate the heretics.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected answer with a new reading of the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה as one continuous rule instead of two clashing rules
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא bans holes completely and the סיפא allows them, so they contradict, or else the רישא is about the marketplace (אביי).
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא bans slaughtering directly into a hole. The סיפא allows slaughtering beside the hole at home, and bans even that in the marketplace.

steps.title: A ברייתא that matches רבא's reading
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא follows רבא's order exactly: a ship case, a full ban on holes, the courtyard method, and a ban in the marketplace based on a פסוק. It adds that whoever does it there must be checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רבא: if someone is on a ship with no room to slaughter, he reaches his hand outside the ship and slaughters, and the blood runs down the side of the ship. One may never slaughter into a hole. To keep a courtyard clean, he makes a spot beside the hole and the blood flows in. In the marketplace he may not do this, because the פסוק says 'ובחקתיהם לא תלכו.' If he did it, people need to look into him afterward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבא said. This shows his reading is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has the same three levels as רבא: a full ban on holes, a courtyard method that is allowed, and a marketplace ban. That shows the marketplace was a separate case and not what the full ban was about, which is רבא's point. It also gives a source from the תורה for the marketplace ban and adds that someone who did it is suspect.

keyTerms.meaning: Ship or boat
The sides or walls of the ship
'Do not follow their practices' (ויקרא 18:3)
Needs to be checked or investigated

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא confirms רבא: never directly into a hole, beside it at home is fine, and not in the marketplace because of 'ובחקתיהם לא תלכו.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns the marketplace ban from a matter of appearances into a ban based on a פסוק, and treats a person who does it as possibly a מין.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita in line with Rava:
If one was traveling on a ship
and he has no room on the ship to slaughter,
he reaches his hand outside the ship and slaughters,

phrases.aramaic: וְדָם שׁוֹתֵת וְיוֹרֵד עַל דּוֹפְנֵי הַסְּפִינָה,
phrases.english: and the blood flows and runs down the sides of the ship.
And one may not slaughter into a hole at all.
And one who wants to keep his courtyard clean,
how does he do it?
He makes a spot outside the hole and slaughters there,
and the blood flows and runs down into the hole.
And in the marketplace he should not do this,
because it says: 'And do not follow their practices,'
and if he did do this,
he needs to be checked afterward.
phrases.notes: People need to look into whether this person is actually a מין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an earlier source that supports רבא's reading from step 8
steps.raayaObject: רבא's reading: a full ban on slaughtering into a hole, the courtyard method allowed, and a marketplace ban
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same structure, plus a ship case and the פסוק 'ובחקתיהם לא תלכו'

steps.title: New משנה: slaughtering for the sake of an offering
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that someone who slaughters an ordinary animal 'for the sake of' a קרבן, such as an עולה, שלמים, אשם תלוי, פסח or תודה, makes his שחיטה invalid. רבי שמעון says it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who slaughters for the sake of an עולה, for the sake of שלמים, for the sake of an אשם תלוי, for the sake of a פסח, or for the sake of a תודה: his שחיטה is invalid. רבי שמעון says it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It asks what happens when someone slaughters an animal and says he is doing it for the sake of a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says the שחיטה is invalid. רבי שמעון disagrees and says it is valid. The משנה only lists the cases and the ruling; the גמרא will work out the reasons next.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt offering
Here: peace offerings (שלמים)
Provisional guilt offering, brought when one is unsure whether he sinned
Thanksgiving offering
Invalid
Rules it valid

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who slaughters for the sake of a burnt offering,
for the sake of peace offerings, for the sake of a provisional guilt offering,
for the sake of a Paschal offering, for the sake of a thanks offering,
his slaughter is invalid,
and Rabbi Shimon rules it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the hole discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering an animal 'for the sake of' a קרבן makes the שחיטה invalid. רבי שמעון rules it valid.

steps.title: Two people slaughtering with one knife
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if two people hold one knife and slaughter together, and one has in mind one of the listed offerings while the other has a proper intention, the שחיטה is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two people hold a knife and slaughter together, one for the sake of one of the offerings listed above and one for a proper purpose, the slaughter is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of rules and adds a case where two people slaughter one animal together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though one of the two had a perfectly proper intention, the other person's bad intention is enough to ruin the whole שחיטה. One bad intention spoils the act, even if it is shared with a good one.

keyTerms.meaning: Holding a knife together
A proper purpose, one that causes no problem
His slaughter is invalid

phrases.english: Two people grasp a knife and slaughter,
one for the sake of one of all these,
phrases.notes: 'These' are the offerings listed just before: עולה, שלמים, אשם תלוי, פסח and תודה.

phrases.english: and one for the sake of a proper thing:
the slaughter is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the ruling in step 10 to a shared שחיטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two people slaughter together and one intends one of the listed offerings, the שחיטה is invalid even though the other's intention was proper.

steps.title: Offerings whose name does not ruin the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: Slaughtering for the sake of a חטאת, אשם ודאי, בכור, מעשר or תמורה leaves the שחיטה valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who slaughters for the sake of a sin offering, a definite guilt offering, a firstborn, animal tithe, or a substitute offering: his slaughter is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second list of offerings. Slaughtering 'for their sake' does not ruin the שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These offerings are the opposite of the first list. A person cannot simply decide to bring them as a gift. They only come from an obligation or happen on their own, so saying their name does not make the animal a real קרבן. The next line spells out this reasoning as a rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering, brought for a known sin
Guilt offering for a definite sin
Firstborn animal, holy from birth
Animal tithe, every tenth animal
An animal swapped for a קרבן, which becomes holy too

phrases.english: One who slaughters for the sake of a sin offering,
for the sake of a definite guilt offering, for the sake of a firstborn,
for the sake of animal tithe, for the sake of a substitute offering:
his slaughter is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite list to step 10: offerings that do not invalidate.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up אשם ודאי (definite guilt offering, listed here as valid) with אשם תלוי (provisional guilt offering, listed in step 10 as invalid).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering an ordinary animal for the sake of a חטאת, אשם ודאי, בכור, מעשר or תמורה leaves the שחיטה valid.

steps.title: The general rule: vow and gift offerings
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up: slaughtering for the sake of any offering that can be vowed or donated is forbidden. Slaughtering for the sake of one that cannot be vowed or donated is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: anything that can be vowed or donated, one who slaughters for its sake makes it forbidden. Anything that cannot be vowed or donated, one who slaughters for its sake makes it valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives one rule that explains both of its lists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dividing line is whether a person can choose to bring the offering as a vow or a gift. If he can, saying its name might really make the animal holy, so it is forbidden. If he cannot, his words do nothing and the שחיטה stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
Can be brought as a vow or as a voluntary gift
For its sake, in its name

steps.whatToRemember: The test is נידר ונידב: offerings a person can choose to bring make the שחיטה forbidden. Offerings that only come from obligation do not.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁנִּידָּר וְנִידָּב –
phrases.english: This is the rule: anything that is vowed and donated,
one who slaughters for its sake, it is forbidden;
and what is not vowed and donated,
one who slaughters for its sake, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the principle behind the two lists in steps 10 and 12.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא's next two questions test the משנה's first list against this rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Offerings that can be vowed or donated make the שחיטה forbidden. Offerings that are only obligations leave it valid.

steps.title: Can an אשם תלוי be donated?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how אשם תלוי can be on the forbidden list. It seems to be only an obligation, not something a person can choose to donate.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who slaughters for the sake of a burnt offering…' But is a provisional guilt offering something that can be vowed or donated?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by quoting the משנה. It points out that אשם תלוי does not seem to fit the rule the משנה just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם תלוי is normally brought because a person is unsure whether he sinned, so it looks like an obligation. By the משנה's own rule, it should belong on the valid list, yet the משנה put it on the forbidden list.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit for, able to be

phrases.english: GEMARA: "One who slaughters for the sake of a burnt offering."
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the משנה to show which part it is discussing.

phrases.aramaic: אָשָׁם תָּלוּי בַּר נִידָּר וְנִידָּב הוּא?
phrases.english: Is a provisional guilt offering something that can be vowed and donated?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָשָׁם תָּלוּי בַּר נִידָּר וְנִידָּב הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the list in step 10 against the rule in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: Listing אשם תלוי among offerings that make the שחיטה forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule forbids only offerings that can be vowed or donated. An אשם תלוי seems to be only an obligation.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the משנה follows רבי אלעזר, who holds that a person may donate an אשם תלוי any day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Whose view is this? It is רבי אלעזר, who says: a person may donate a provisional guilt offering every day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question by saying which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר, an אשם תלוי can also be a voluntary offering, brought just in case. So it does count as נידר ונידב, and it fits the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
Donates voluntarily
Every day

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Whose view is this?
It is Rabbi Elazar, who says:

phrases.aramaic: מִתְנַדֵּב אָדָם אָשָׁם תָּלוּי בְּכׇל יוֹם.
phrases.english: A person may donate a provisional guilt offering every day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An אשם תלוי is only an obligation and cannot be donated.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי אלעזר, for whom an אשם תלוי can be donated daily. So it is נידר ונידב.

steps.title: Can a פסח be donated?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a פסח can be on the forbidden list. It has a fixed date and seems to be only an obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a פסח something that can be vowed or donated? It has a fixed time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the same kind of question about a second item on the forbidden list, the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסח is brought only on its set day as a required offering, not whenever a person wants to donate. So it seems to fail the נידר ונידב test.

keyTerms.meaning: Paschal offering
It has a fixed time

phrases.english: Is a Paschal offering something that can be donated and vowed?
It has a fixed time!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same type of question as step 14, now about the פסח.
steps.kashyaTarget: Listing פסח among offerings that make the שחיטה forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסח has a fixed date and is an obligation, so it does not seem to be נידר ונידב.

steps.title: The פסח can be set aside all year
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא answers that פסח is different, because a person can set it aside at any time during the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: The פסח is different, since it can be set aside the whole year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא explains why the פסח still counts for the משנה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though it is offered only on its fixed day, a person can set aside an animal for it at any time of year. Because he can set it aside whenever he wants, saying the name 'פסח' could make the animal holy. So it is treated like a נידר ונידב offering.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
Since, because
Setting aside an animal for a קרבן

steps.whatToRemember: Both hard cases fit the rule. אשם תלוי fits because רבי אלעזר holds it can be donated daily. פסח fits because it can be set aside all year.

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said: The Paschal offering is different,
since setting it aside can be done the entire year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing a special feature of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the פסח has a fixed date, it is only an obligation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסח can be set aside any time of year, so it is treated like a vowed or donated offering.

steps.title: רבי ינאי: The rule is only about unblemished animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי says the משנה's problem with slaughtering 'for the sake of an offering' applies only to unblemished animals. With a blemished animal, everyone knows it cannot be an offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי says: The משנה's rule applies only to unblemished animals. With blemished animals, everyone already knows they cannot be offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי limits the משנה's rule. Slaughtering 'for the sake of an עולה' and similar offerings is a problem only when the animal is fit to be an offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry in the משנה is that this person might really mean the animal as an offering. A blemished animal cannot be brought as an offering, and this is obvious. So nobody would think his words are serious, and there is no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught this about...': a phrase that limits a משנה's rule to a narrower case
Unblemished animals, fit to be offerings
Animals with a blemish, which cannot be brought as offerings
'It is surely known': it is obvious to everyone

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai says:
They only taught this about unblemished animals,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the משנה's rule that slaughtering 'for the sake of an עולה' and similar offerings is a problem.

phrases.english: but with blemished animals —
it is surely known.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא תְּמִימִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how far the משנה's rule reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The problem applies only to unblemished animals. Blemished animals are known to be unfit, so slaughtering them this way is not a problem.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Even blemished animals are included
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees: the problem applies even to blemished animals, because sometimes the blemish is covered and nobody can see it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן says: Even blemished animals are included, because sometimes something is lying over the blemish and nobody knows it is there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן argues with רבי ינאי and says the rule covers blemished animals too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי relied on the blemish being obvious. רבי יוחנן points out that a blemish can be hidden, for example by something lying over it. Then people would not know the animal is unfit, so the same worry returns.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes
The blemish
Lies on, is thrown over

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says:
even blemished animals are included too,
since sometimes something lies on the blemish
and it is not known.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רבי ינאי in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blemished animals are also included, since the blemish may be hidden and people may not know about it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Slaughtering 'for a חטאת' is valid only if he does not owe one
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says slaughtering 'for the sake of a חטאת' is valid. רבי יוחנן limits this to a person who does not owe a חטאת. If he does owe one, we worry he means it as his real חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: About one who slaughters for the sake of a חטאת, רבי יוחנן says: They only taught that it is valid when he does not owe a חטאת. But if he owes a חטאת, we say he is doing it for the sake of his own חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of slaughtering 'for the sake of a חטאת', and רבי יוחנן limits when that slaughter is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת cannot be donated, so normally nobody would think the person is serious. A person who actually owes a חטאת is different: his words could really mean his own required חטאת. Then the slaughter is a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering, which a person brings only when he is required to, never as a donation
A person who owes, or is required to bring, a חטאת
'Say': we might assume

phrases.english: One who slaughters for the sake of a sin offering,
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which said this slaughter is valid.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחוּיָּיב חַטָּאת,
phrases.english: They only taught this when he does not owe a sin offering,
but if he owes a sin offering —
say he is doing it for the sake of his own sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׁוֹחֵט לְשֵׁם חַטָּאת, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה: slaughtering for the sake of a חטאת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering 'for the sake of a חטאת' is valid only when the person does not owe a חטאת.

steps.title: But he did not say 'my חטאת'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: the person only said 'for a חטאת', not 'for my חטאת', so why worry?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he did not say, 'For the sake of my חטאת'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man's words were general: 'a חטאת'. That does not point to the specific חטאת he owes, so it seems there is no reason to think he meant his own required offering.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But he did not say...': a challenge based on the exact words used
'My sin offering'

phrases.english: But he did not say, 'For the sake of my sin offering'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's limit from Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that a person who owes a חטאת is suspected of meaning his own חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His words were general and did not mention his own חטאת, so there should be no suspicion.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: He did say 'my חטאת'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that רבי יוחנן is talking about a case where the person actually said 'for the sake of my חטאת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: It is talking about one who says, 'For the sake of my חטאת.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the challenge by explaining which case רבי יוחנן means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's case is one where the person said 'my חטאת'. Since he really owes one, his words could truly mean his own offering, and that is why the slaughter is a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In a case where he says': sets the exact case being discussed

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
It is where he says, 'For the sake of my sin offering.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן seemed to be talking about someone who just said 'a חטאת'.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן's rule is about someone who owes a חטאת and said 'my חטאת'.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: Slaughtering 'for a תמורה' is valid only if he has no offering at home
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says slaughtering 'for the sake of a תמורה' is valid. רבי אלעזר limits this to someone who has no consecrated animal at home. If he has one, we worry he is making this animal its substitute.
steps.simpleTranslation: About slaughtering for the sake of a תמורה, רבי אלעזר says: They only taught that it is valid when he has no offering in his house. But if he has an offering in his house, say he is substituting this animal for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of slaughtering 'for the sake of a תמורה', and רבי אלעזר limits when it is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תמורה is an animal that takes on holiness when someone tries to swap it for an animal that is already an offering. If the person has no offering, there is nothing to swap with, so his words mean nothing. If he does have one, his words could really make this animal its substitute.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute: an animal that someone tries to swap for an animal already set aside as an offering, which also becomes holy
An offering, here an animal already set aside as an offering
'He is substituting it for it': he is making this animal a substitute for his offering

phrases.english: For the sake of a substitute,
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which said slaughtering for the sake of a תמורה is valid.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין לוֹ זֶבַח בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: They only taught this when he has no offering in his house,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יֵשׁ לוֹ זֶבַח בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ –
phrases.english: but if he has an offering in his house —
say he is substituting it for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְשֵׁם תְּמוּרָה, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה, following the same pattern as Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering 'for the sake of a תמורה' is valid only when the person has no offering at home that this animal could replace.

steps.title: But he did not say 'substitute for my offering'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר: the person said only 'for a תמורה', not 'for a substitute for my offering'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he did not say, 'For the sake of a substitute for my offering'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question it asked on the חטאת case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His general words did not mention the offering he has at home. So why should we think he meant to swap this animal for it?

keyTerms.meaning: 'A substitute for my offering'

phrases.english: But he did not say, 'For the sake of a substitute for my offering'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's limit from Step 23, the same way Step 21 challenged Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that a person with an offering at home is suspected of making a substitute for it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His words were general and did not mention his own offering.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: He did say 'substitute for my offering'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו again answers that the case is one where the person actually said 'for the sake of a substitute for my offering'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: It is talking about one who says, 'For the sake of a substitute for my offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives the same kind of answer he gave for the חטאת case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר is talking about someone who pointed to his own offering. Because he has one at home, his words could really create a תמורה, so the slaughter is a problem.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
It is where he says, 'For the sake of a substitute for my offering.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: בְּאוֹמֵר ״לְשֵׁם תְּמוּרַת זִבְחִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר seemed to be talking about someone who just said 'a תמורה'.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר's rule is about someone who has an offering at home and said 'a substitute for my offering'.
steps.whatToRemember: The rules for חטאת and תמורה follow the same pattern. The slaughter is valid unless the person could truly have such an offering and he pointed to his own one with the word 'my'.

steps.title: What does 'זה הכלל' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra case the משנה's words 'זה הכלל' ('this is the rule') are meant to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This is the rule': what does it come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה needed to add a general rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already listed specific cases. A general rule usually comes to add a case the list did not mention, so the גמרא asks what that case is.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is the rule': a general summary in a משנה
'To include what?': asking which extra case a phrase adds

phrases.english: 'This is the rule' —
phrases.notes: These are the משנה's words from Step 13: if someone slaughters for the sake of an offering that can be vowed or donated, the animal is forbidden.

phrases.english: what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's general rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case, not listed in the משנה, is included by 'זה הכלל'.

steps.title: It includes the עולה of a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The rule includes slaughtering 'for the sake of a נזיר's עולה'. You might think it is fine because this person never became a נזיר, but he might have made the vow in private.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include the עולה of a נזיר. You might have said: this man never vowed to be a נזיר, so there is no worry. So the rule teaches: say he vowed in private.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'זה הכלל' adds the case of a נזיר's עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר's עולה is required only of someone who took a נזיר vow, and this man is not known to be a נזיר. Still, a נזיר vow is something a person chooses, and it can be made privately. So we worry he really is a נזיר and means this as his real offering.

keyTerms.meaning: The עולה (burnt offering) a נזיר brings at the end of his נזירות
'You might have said': introduces a mistaken idea that the teaching comes to correct
In private, secretly

phrases.english: To include the burnt offering of a nazirite,
for you might have said:
'This man did not vow,'
phrases.notes: He means: he never vowed to be a נזיר, so you might think there is nothing to worry about.

phrases.english: say he vowed in private.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'זה הכלל' includes slaughtering for the sake of a נזיר's עולה, because he may have taken a נזיר vow in private.
steps.whatToRemember: Slaughtering 'for the sake of a נזיר's עולה' is forbidden, even if nobody knows of a vow, because he may have vowed in private.

steps.title: What does the second half of the rule include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the second half of the משנה's rule, 'and that is not vowed or donated,' to ask what extra case it comes to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the part of the rule that says 'an offering that is not vowed or donated': what does it come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה's general rule and asks what new case it adds. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 26 the גמרא asked what the first part of 'זה הכלל' includes. Now it asks the same about the second part: offerings a person must bring by obligation, not by choice. The question words are left out and only the quote appears, but it works as a question.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings a person brings by choice, either by a vow (נדר) or as a gift (נדבה)
An offering that is not brought by choice. It is an obligation.

phrases.english: And [the part of the rule about an offering] that is not vowed or donated,
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves the question unsaid. It means: what does this part of the rule come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the question pattern of step 26, now for the second half of 'זה הכלל'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which extra case the phrase 'שאינו נידר ונידב' in the משנה's rule comes to include.

steps.title: It includes a woman's birth offering
steps.stepSummary: The phrase comes to include slaughtering an animal 'for the sake of a woman's birth offering' (עולת יולדת). That slaughter is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include the burnt offering of a woman who gave birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this part of the rule covers someone who slaughters 'for the sake of a woman's birth offering.' The slaughter is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who gives birth must bring an עולה. It is an obligation, not a voluntary gift. Since nobody would bring such an offering on a whim, saying its name while slaughtering a regular animal does not make the slaughter forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: To include (an extra case)
The burnt offering a woman must bring after giving birth

phrases.english: To include the burnt offering of a woman after childbirth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second half of the rule includes slaughtering for the sake of an עולת יולדת. That slaughter is valid.

steps.title: Valid only if he has no wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר limits the ruling: it is valid only if the man has no wife. If he has a wife, we worry he is slaughtering for her offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: They taught this only when he has no wife. But if he has a wife, we can say he is doing it for her sake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר puts a limit on the ruling. It is valid only for a man with no wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same pattern as step 23 with the תמורה. If the man has a wife, she might really need to bring a birth offering. Then his words could mean he is making this animal her real offering, and that is a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in the case of... (a limiting phrase)
Say / we can suspect that...
For her sake (here: for his wife's offering)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אִשָּׁה,
phrases.english: They taught this only where he has no wife,
but if he has a wife,
say that he is doing it for her sake.
phrases.notes: He means for the sake of his wife's real birth offering, so the slaughter would not be valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of step 29, just as רבי אלעזר limited the תמורה case in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering for an עולת יולדת is valid only if the man has no wife. If he has one, we suspect he means her offering.

steps.title: But he didn't say 'my wife'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר: the man said only 'a woman's birth offering,' not 'my wife's offering,' so why worry?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he did not say 'for the sake of my wife's burnt offering'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אלעזר. The man's words were general and never mentioned his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same challenge as step 24. If he spoke only about some general birth offering, there is no reason to tie his words to his own wife.

keyTerms.meaning: But he did not say... (introduces a challenge)
My wife

phrases.english: But he did not say
'for the sake of my wife's burnt offering'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's limit from step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's worry that the man means his wife's offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The man's words were general ('a woman's birth offering'), so nothing links them to his own wife.

steps.title: He did say 'my wife's offering'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that the case is one where the man really said 'for the sake of my wife's burnt offering.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: The case is where he says 'for the sake of my wife's burnt offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו defends רבי אלעזר by changing the case. The man did mention his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same answer רבי אבהו gave in step 25. Once he says 'my wife,' his words point to a real offering his wife may owe, so the worry makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where he says...

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
It is where he says 'for the sake of my wife's burnt offering.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The man spoke only generally about a birth offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: He explicitly said 'my wife's burnt offering', so it points to a real offering she may owe.

steps.title: Then it is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רבי אבהו's answer: if he clearly said 'my wife,' of course the slaughter is not valid. Why would רבי אלעזר need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבהו's answer. If the man said 'my wife' outright, the law is so clear that nobody needed to teach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making the case so explicit removes the challenge of step 31 but creates a new problem. A ruling about such a clear case seems to teach nothing new. The גמרא will need to show why it still had to be said.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a ruling teaches nothing new)

steps.confusionAlert: פשיטא does not mean the גמרא agrees. It is an attack: a teaching that only states the obvious is suspicious, and the גמרא expects an answer.

phrases.english: Is it not obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's explanation of רבי אלעזר's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the man explicitly said 'my wife's offering', the slaughter is clearly not valid, so רבי אלעזר's ruling would be pointless.
